summary: Owner-ruled correction set for Unity GCSE Geography Paper 1 (20 lessons). Item 1: the Cumbria 2009 cost breakdown (129.2+98.3+34+12.9 = 274.4, not 276.5) and the government-plus-insurance sums are removed; the one cost figure kept is the ~275 million pound damage bill, relabelled from 'insurance cost' across the lesson because the verified insurance payout was 174 million pounds (ABI, 25,000 claims) while 276 million pounds is the total Cumbria damage bill (Cumbria County Council, one year on). Item 2: the oxygen claim is corrected in 3 places, not 4 - it appears in lesson 11 content and conclusion and in one lesson 10 mark scheme; no other field in the unit carries it. Item 3: beach nourishment now reads per 100 metres, matching the dune figure. Item 4: all 20 descriptions rewritten to 85-97 characters. No Supabase write performed.

item1_cumbria_costs.evidence: Cumbria County Council one-year-on figure ~276m total damage bill; ABI 25,000 claims and 174m pounds paid (4ni.co.uk 19 Nov 2010). Wikipedia 2009 Great Britain and Ireland floods gives only contemporary estimates over 100m pounds.
item1_cumbria_costs.note: Departure from the literal ruling: the ruling said to keep 'insurance claims of around 275 million'. 275 million is verified as the TOTAL damage bill, not insurance, so the figure is kept and the label corrected everywhere. No answer key value changes - the knowledge check answer stays 275.

item2_oxygen.note: Ruling said four fields; only three occurrences exist in this unit (grep for oxygen / lungs / 20% of the world).

item3_beach_nourishment.note: 3,000 pounds per kilometre became per 100 metres, consistent with the dune figure of 2,000 pounds per 100 metres in the same lesson.
